text: When an ECP5 CORDIC is timing-limited at 194.4 MHz by the carry-chain in each micro-rotation stage, drop guard bits from 2 to 0 and iterations from 16 to 12 to shorten the adder chain, saving 796 LUTs and making 200 MHz feasible (+5.6 MHz) at 12-bit precision.

When an ECP5 CORDIC is pinned at its 200 MHz constraint by a 16-bit carry chain (1.35 ns logic + 1.76 ns route), do not cut pipelined stages from 12 to 10 just to save 333 LUTs—Fmax fell to 199.84 MHz and lost feasibility because the per-stage carry chain stayed critical and routing/placement worsened; cut stages only if Fmax has slack or also split/shorten the carry chain.

When an ECP5 CORDIC is timing-limited by the 16-bit carry-chain adder path (FF→16-cell chain→LUT4→FF) rather than stage count, don't cut iterations from 10 to 8 to fix Fmax: it saves 328 LUTs but leaves the same carry-chain critical path and costs 4.3 MHz (199.8→195.5), so pipeline/split the adder or improve its placement instead.

When the ECP5 CORDIC is stuck at 195.5 MHz on a 16-cell carry-chain stage whose ~2.9 ns is dominated by routing, do not add micro-rotation iterations—going 8→11 added 494 LUT (1261→1755) and 0 DSP while Fmax rose only 5.7 MHz to 201.2 MHz because placement shrank carry-chain route from 2.0 ns to 1.47 ns—so instead cut iterations or fold to reduce LUT until placement clears 200 MHz.

For an ECP5 CORDIC pinned near 201 MHz by a 16-cell carry-chain stage (~5.0 ns, FF+carry+LUT), cut pipeline iterations from 11 to 9 to save 327 LUT with no Fmax gain (201.25→201.29 MHz), since the single carry-chain stage, not stage count, sets the period.

When an ECP5 CORDIC is feasible but pinned by a 4.97 ns FF→15-cell carry-chain→LUT4 adder stage, cut micro-rotation iterations from 9 to 6 at unroll=1/guard=0 to remove ~501 LUT (1428→927) while the same per-stage adder path becomes 4.85 ns, gaining +4.9 MHz (201.3→206.2 MHz) because Fmax is set by the single 16-bit adder, not the number of stages.

When an ECP5 unrolled CORDIC is LUT-heavy but timing is flat across iteration counts because each micro-rotation stage is bounded by a 15-cell 16-bit carry-chain adder (1.32 ns logic + 1.47 ns route), cut iterations from 6 to 4 to save 333 LUT (927→594) while gaining 5.6 MHz (206.2→211.8 MHz), since Fmax is set by the per-stage carry chain rather than the number of stages.

When an ECP5 CORDIC is carry-chain-limited at ~212 MHz and max_dsp=0, keep the micro-rotation iteration count at 4 rather than adding a fifth stage, because the extra stage costs +167 LUT for 0 DSP and drops Fmax to 205.6 MHz while the period is set by the single 15–16-cell carry-chain adder per stage, not by iteration count.

When an ECP5 CORDIC is timing-limited at 59.3 MHz by unroll=4 chaining four carry-chain micro-rotations into a 16.88 ns path, collapse unroll 4->1, cut iterations 16->12, and trim guard bits 2->0 to shorten the carry chain and remove adder/register columns, reaching 200 MHz and saving 789 LUTs at 0 DSP.

When an ECP5 CORDIC sits at a zero-margin 200 MHz with its critical path in a 16-cell carry chain and only LUT is movable, cut micro-rotation iterations from 12 to 4 to reach 594 LUT and 211.8 MHz (+11.8 MHz) at fold=1, because the shorter carry/select path is timing-critical while DSP and throughput stay unchanged.

On an ECP5 CORDIC whose timing is set by a 15-cell carry-chain adder, do not increase iterations from 4 to 6—it added 333 LUT and dropped Fmax by 5.6 MHz (211.8→206.2) with no DSP or feasibility gain—because the carry chain, not iteration count, sets the period; instead shorten or retime the adder or keep iterations low.

When an ECP5 CORDIC rotate misses 200 MHz because a 16-cell carry chain (1.39 ns logic + 1.72 ns route) plus a LUT4 shift bounds the stage, cut iterations 16→10 and guard bits 2→0 to shrink the adder chain to 11 cells, yielding +5.5 MHz (to 199.8 MHz) and -1129 LUT, though still short of target.

When an ECP5 CORDIC misses 200 MHz at 199.84 MHz with an 11-cell carry chain on x_q[3], changing micro-rotation iterations from 10 to 12 (+333 LUT, +0 DSP) moved the critical path to a 16-cell y_q[2] carry chain but shortened the LUT4 route from 1.23 ns to 1.00 ns, clearing 200 MHz (+0.2 MHz), so test iteration-count retiming before assuming extra stages only add delay.

On an ECP5 CORDIC whose 200.0 MHz period is set by a single 16-cell carry-chain micro-rotation stage, cut micro-rotation stages from 12 to 4 to remove 1328 LUT (1922->594) and lift Fmax to 211.8 MHz because reducing stage count shrinks routing congestion around that per-stage carry chain rather than shortening the adder itself.

On an ECP5 CORDIC that is feasible at 211.8 MHz with 594 LUT and a 16-bit carry-chain micro-rotation adder as the critical path, do not increase iterations from 4 to 6 for extra precision, because it adds 333 LUT and drops Fmax 5.6 MHz to 206.2 MHz while still feasible, since the period stays set by one 16-bit carry-chain stage and extra stages only add parallel LUT/carry logic.

When an ECP5 CORDIC at 0 DSP is feasible at ~206 MHz with 927 LUTs and its critical path is a 15-cell 16-bit carry chain plus LUT4, do not fold four pipelined iteration stages into one reused adder, because the added variable-shift/feedback LUT4 + carry-chain path lengthens the critical path to 8.13 ns and drops Fmax to 123 MHz despite saving 546 LUTs.

When an ECP5 CORDIC at unroll 1 is timing-limited by a 16-cell carry chain at 194.4 MHz, cut iterations 16->12 and guard bits 2->0 to shorten the carry chain and remove adder/register columns, freeing ~800 LUTs and clearing 200 MHz (+5.6 MHz) at 1 sample/cycle.

On ECP5 CORDIC at a zero-margin 200 MHz with a single 16-cell carry-chain micro-rotation adder setting the period, cut micro-rotations from 12 to 4 to remove 1328 LUT (1922->594) and lift Fmax 11.8 MHz to 211.8 MHz by decongesting routing around the unchanged per-stage carry chain.

When an ECP5 CORDIC is feasible but zero-margin with a single 16-cell carry-chain micro-rotation adder as the critical path, going from 4 to 6 iterations adds 333 LUTs and drops Fmax from 211.8 to 206.2 MHz with no DSP change, because the extra stages only worsen routing around the same 5-ns FF→carry→LUT→FF path; keep 4 iterations unless netlist simulation fails.

When an ECP5 CORDIC's 16-cell carry-chain micro-rotation limits it to 194.4 MHz, cut guard bits 2→0 and iterations 16→12 to shorten the adder and remove four columns, reaching 200 MHz (+5.6 MHz) while dropping 796 LUTs at 1 sample/cycle.

When an ECP5 CORDIC is timing-limited by a route-dominated 16-cell carry-chain micro-rotation stage at ~200 MHz, cut iterations from 12 to 4 to decongest routing around that unchanged carry chain, raising Fmax to 211.8 MHz and reducing LUTs from 1922 to 594 with no DSP change.

When an ECP5 CORDIC is near the 200 MHz feasibility limit with a route-dominated FF->16-bit carry-chain->LUT4 micro-rotation critical path, keep the iteration stage count at the minimum (e.g., 4) rather than increasing it to 6, because the extra stages add 333 LUTs and drop Fmax by 5.6 MHz (211.8→206.2) by increasing routing congestion around the fixed carry chain without shortening the per-stage path.

When an ECP5 CORDIC is timing-limited by a FF→16-cell carry-chain→LUT4→FF path where carry-chain and post-adder LUT routing dominate, shorten the adder by dropping guard bits 2→0 and cut micro-rotation iterations 16→12 to relieve fabric congestion, gaining +5.6 MHz (194.4→200 MHz) and -796 LUTs at 0 DSPs.

When an ECP5 CORDIC is routing-limited at a zero-margin 200 MHz by an unchanged 16-cell carry-chain plus LUT4 mux in one micro-rotation stage and the 16-bit width/guard_bits leave no arithmetic to shorten, cut micro-rotation columns from 12 to the legal minimum of 4 to drop ~1,328 LUTs and decongest routing around that same carry chain (+11.8 MHz to 211.8 MHz, DSP unchanged).

When an ECP5 CORDIC violates timing at 59 MHz because unroll=4 serializes four micro-rotation carry chains (17/11/16/17 cells) into a 16.9 ns path, collapse unroll to 1, drop guard bits 2→0, and trim iterations 16→11, which shortens the critical carry chain to 16 cells and reaches 201 MHz while cutting 956 LUTs.

When an ECP5 CORDIC is already feasible at ~201 MHz with a 16-cell carry chain dominating, keep the iteration count at 11 instead of 12, since the 12th micro-rotation iteration adds 167 LUT and drops Fmax to 200 MHz while leaving the carry-chain critical path unchanged.

On ECP5 CORDIC designs that are feasible but limited by a ~5 ns 16-cell carry-chain adder with routing-dominated delay, cut iterations from 12 to the legal minimum 4 to remove 1328 LUTs (1922→594) and decongest routing, shortening the same carry-chain path to ~4.72 ns and lifting Fmax 200→211.8 MHz with no DSP change.

On an ECP5 CORDIC with a feasible carry-chain-critical design, do not raise iterations from 4 to 6: it adds 333 LUTs and drops Fmax 5.6 MHz (211.8→206.2 MHz) while staying feasible, because the per-stage carry-chain adder remains the critical path, so keep the iteration count at the legal minimum unless accuracy requires more.
